v4-01.acceptance: The whole program builds and passes its full gate with the window toolkit absent from its dependency graph, and no check anywhere starts a window or audits one. What must still hold without the window: every function Conductor had — describing, starting, following, reading and cleaning up a run, and the capability coverage view — is exercised from the command line in that same gate, and the masters say in plain words that Conductor has no interface.

v4-02.acceptance: A search of the tree for anything that names a model of Pulse's, real or canned, among scenarios, contracts, launch terms, postures, verdicts, report states, tests and scripts finds only the dated records of what was measured, each marked closed with the model it graded. What must still hold without it: every detection the engine keeps is still proven by a run, and the full gate is green with no model term anywhere in the path a run takes.

v4-03.acceptance: A run of every kind completes from its first line to its last with no person present and nothing waiting for one, and the tree holds no hold, no checklist, no manual state or lamp, no drive-and-observe class, no contract or harvest about a window's timing and no scenario whose subject is a window. What must still hold without them: every outcome a run reports is one a machine gave, and a run with nothing to grade still ends with a stated outcome that is not a failure.

v4-04.acceptance: A run against an engine succeeds given only that engine's address and credentials, on one machine and on two through the same network path, while Conductor reads no file of the engine's, starts no process of the engine's, binds no port of the engine's and shares no directory, key or environment with it; no scenario, fault, contract term, precondition or suite has a shared machine as its subject. What must still hold without the shared machine: every proof of a kept detection that used to read the engine's log file has a run read through the door in its place, and that run existed before the proof left.

v4-05.acceptance: Every run reports its timing per event — how long after an event's onset the engine reported it — and no tier, no per-scenario latency and no exception list for one appears in a run description, a run record or a report. The load a run is held to is a figure measured against the engine with its store on disk, and it admits a run of hours. What must still hold without the tiers: a run that exceeds the measured load bound is still told apart from evidence about the engine.

v4-06.acceptance: Conductor's accepted set, its classification and its coverage record match Pulse's re-based capability record entry for entry and name no capability Pulse has retired; every run and every scheduled event names the capability of the engine it exercises; the pinned references are Pulse's current ones; nothing in the set was written before Pulse's record existed. What must still hold without the old pin: a run that names a capability outside the set is refused, a capability claimed as automatically checked has a run that names it, and at the version's close the two projects' sets agree.

v4-07.acceptance: Conductor builds, passes its full gate and completes a run on Linux, and neither the tree nor its hosted checks hold a script or a leg for another operating system. What must still hold without the other systems: every gate the earlier hosted checks enforced — tests, the coverage floor, zero retries, supply chain, secret scan, the static gates and the own-log gates — is still enforced, and each can be run on the developer's host before a push.

v4-08.acceptance: Each record a newcomer or an agent reads first — the project's instructions, its description, its brief, the architecture and security masters and the always-loaded rules — describes a console harness that drives an engine on another host over a network with credentials it holds, and a reading of every rule finds none that instructs a thing this version removes or forbids a thing it adds. What must still hold: the dated history of what earlier versions were stays readable as history.

v4-09.acceptance: A run is started, followed while it runs and read after it ends from the command line alone, and every status it shows is carried by a text label.

v4-10.acceptance: A run sends its stream to an engine on another host with a token over an encrypted channel, and the same path carries a run when both programs are on one machine. A token is never sent to another host over a plain channel, and an engine whose identity cannot be verified is refused before anything is sent to it. What the engine is verified against is given to the run together with the address, and where it comes from is stated.

v4-11.acceptance: After a run against an engine that admitted it, neither the engine's token nor the door's credential appears in the run description, the run record, the journal, the report, the logs or what the console printed. A run whose credential the engine rejects is reported as blocked, not as a failed check. The place a run reads its credentials from is stated and is outside the repository. The engine's address appears in no committed artifact, and a run's record names its engine by the label the operator gave it. Conductor holds no credential of a model's, and the security master rates Conductor as a program that holds credentials and reaches another host.

v4-12.acceptance: Every reading of the engine — its findings, its one-line status and the record of each notification it raised — comes through the door the investigating agent uses. Before a run, a gate proves through that path that the engine is reachable, that it admits Conductor, and that a canary event sent now comes back as a finding; each unmet proof is reported under its own name, and nothing is sent to an engine that has not admitted Conductor. A run's record states the engine state it started from and tells what the engine already held apart from what the run raised; the door's one write is used only where a run needs it and is named as a write. Checks that need an engine run on the dev host and on the two-host run and leave run records; the hosted checks run only what claims Conductor's own behaviour, say so, and hold no credential of an engine's.

v4-13.acceptance: A run's world holds three to five named services with call links between them, each carrying a version, and a fault placed in one service shows in the telemetry of another service that calls it.

v4-14.acceptance: Between a run's events the world keeps emitting a traffic curve with a compressed day, ordinary noise and harmless errors at a low rate, the same stream for the same seed; a healthy hour of it sent to an engine is graded nothing reported.

v4-15.acceptance: A whole run has one timeline, and events scheduled on it overlap across services. The first long run holds the four families: a silent death, a slow creep, periodic spikes, and a break after a change delivered as a new version of a service that starts failing. For the slow families the reading not reported is recorded as the measured starting point, not as a miss.

v4-16.acceptance: A run is described only as a world and a schedule of declared events. Every detection the engine still claims has a short run in that form — one scheduled event, its truth declared, its reaction read through the door — and each of the three unclear subjects either has such a run or is gone, as Pulse's re-based record decides. The single-list scenario form and every file in it are gone. What must still hold without them: no proof of a kept detection was lost, because each had its replacing run before its old form left.

v4-17.acceptance: Every scheduled event declares what it is, in which service, from which minute, and what a correct reaction names; every healthy stretch declares that nothing should be reported; a run description that lacks any of these is refused.

v4-18.acceptance: Every regression run has a paired control that differs from it in exactly one declared thing, and the two are graded differently. For a detection, the same world without the event is graded nothing reported. For a subject whose correct reaction is silence, the control keeps the event, removes what should silence it, and is graded reported. A run whose assertion would also hold in its control is refused when the run is described.

v4-19.acceptance: A run's record keeps, for each reaction, when the engine spoke and the structured facts it named — service, version, kind of finding, error identity, evidence identifiers — placed on the run's timeline. The content boundary is stated for a world whose facts are Conductor's own names coming back, and the exception once written for a model's text no longer exists.

v4-20.acceptance: For a whole run the grading states which planted events were caught, how many minutes after their onset, how many reports came per hour of healthy stretch, and whether each report named the declared service and cause, with both timelines laid on one stated time base. The difference between the two hosts' clocks is measured, and a verdict that difference could change is reported as such. Every verdict is one a machine gave.

v4-21.acceptance: A run of ten hours or more completes against the console engine on a host with no graphics processor and ends with its graded timeline. It reads the engine's memory against the one-gigabyte target and the growth of its database file through the door, as part of the engine's own state, never from a file or a process of the engine's. The run's own record, journal and log are written as the run goes, stay bounded in memory, and stay within a stated bound on disk over the ten hours. A run interrupted at any hour leaves a readable record of everything that happened until then.

v4-22.acceptance: The emitted stream of a recorded run, replayed to the engine faster than it was recorded, produces the same reactions as the original run.

v4-23.acceptance: On a real two-host run Conductor rolls out a bad version of one service in its world; the engine's status line and its report name the service, the version and the new error; the developer's own agent, given the report and the door, names the planted cause, and Conductor records that answer against the declared truth. The answer comes back through a command, bounded in size and scrubbed before it is recorded; Conductor starts no agent and holds no model credential, and the engine calls no model. The answer is recorded as a reading and can fail no build.

v4-24.acceptance: At the close the question is asked of the whole tree — what stands that exists only for a window, Conductor's or Pulse's, for Pulse's local model, for a shared machine, for another operating system or for a human in the loop — and the recorded answer, with the search that produced it, is nothing. What must still hold: the full gate is green and every other capability of this version is verified on measured evidence.
